one_line: Last Hindu ruler of medieval Kashmir, a capable queen-regent who governed Srinagar and Andarkot until Shah Mir’s takeover in 1339.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s, slender but strong build, poised and athletic rather than delicate.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, light wheatish Kashmiri complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes with slightly arched brows, a thin beauty mark near the left cheekbone; default expression calm and calculating with a subtle, dignified half-smile.
appearance.hair: Long straight black hair parted slightly off-center, pulled back into a low, neat bun at the nape wrapped with a muted gold cloth band; a slim, era-accurate silver hairpin with a small lotus-shaped top securing the bun, no loose strands over the face.
appearance.costume: She wears a full-length Kashmiri-style ankle-length gown resembling an early pheran: soft woolen fabric in deep indigo blue, straight long sleeves and modest round neck, hem and cuffs edged with fine saffron-colored border; over it a sleeveless, hip-length quilted vest in muted maroon with simple repetitive lozenge quilting, tied at the front with narrow gold cords; a pale cream woolen stole with faint vine motifs in light green draped over both shoulders and crossing in front; lower body covered by loose straight trousers in earthy brown tucked into soft leather shoes dyed dark brown; jewelry limited to a pair of small gold hoop earrings, a thin gold necklace with a single round pendant, and a simple gold bangle on each wrist.
appearance.signature: A rolled parchment map of Srinagar and Andarkot held firmly in her left hand, bound with a red cord and sealed with a small clay seal, symbolizing her rule and strategic governance.

ref_desc: Kota Rani is a wheatish-complexioned Kashmiri queen in an indigo gown, maroon quilted vest, cream stole, brown trousers and shoes, with a low-bun wrapped in gold cloth, silver lotus hairpin, simple gold jewelry, and a red-tied parchment map in hand.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Kota Rani: an early-30s Kashmiri queen with an oval face, wheatish complexion, sharp dark eyes and calm, calculating expression. Her long black hair is parted slightly off-center and pulled into a low bun wrapped with a muted gold cloth band, secured by a slim silver hairpin topped with a small lotus shape. She wears an ankle-length, straight-sleeved Kashmiri-style woolen gown in deep indigo blue with fine saffron-colored borders at hem and cuffs, over which sits a sleeveless, hip-length muted maroon quilted vest tied at the front with narrow gold cords. A pale cream woolen stole with faint light-green vine motifs is draped over both shoulders and crossed in front, and her lower body is covered by loose straight earthy-brown trousers tucked into dark brown soft leather shoes. Her jewelry is modest: small gold hoop earrings, a thin gold necklace with a single round pendant, and one simple gold bangle on each wrist. In her left hand she grips a rolled parchment map of Srinagar and Andarkot bound with a red cord and marked with a small clay seal, emphasizing her role as a strategic ruler; keep the colors dominated by indigo blue, saffron yellow, muted maroon, cream, and earthy brown, and present her in a neutral standing pose suitable as a consistent reference sheet.
